session.question: How FT's do they add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements when they fulfill their boundary-spanning role?
session.answer:
First-tier suppliers (FTs) add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements while fulfilling their boundary-spanning role due to the influence of their cognitive and relational capital developed with the focal firm. This intermediary position enables FTs to navigate and apply sustainability mandates in ways that align with both their understanding and the specific contexts of the second-tier suppliers (STs) they engage with. The study differentiates between compliance-oriented actions, where FTs adhere strictly to external sustainability requirements, and improvement-oriented actions, where they inject their interpretations to enhance sustainability initiatives (unknownauthorsUnknownyeartheboundaryspanningrole chunk 1).

The relationship dynamics between FTs and focal firms substantially affect their approaches to sustainability requirements. Stronger relational ties and cognitive engagement may lead FTs to be more innovative in how they integrate and communicate these requirements to STs. Evidence suggests that the operational context and the type of relationship foster advanced interpretations and implementations of sustainability (unknownauthorsUnknownyeartheboundaryspanningrole chunk 1). Thus, the boundary-spanning role, coupled with a nuanced understanding of relational dynamics, cultivates a framework through which FTs can personalize sustainability mandates to foster broader organizational goals (unknownauthorsUnknownyeartheboundaryspanningrole chunk 1).
